root_cause_verification.rationale: Root cause was dual: (1) independent subagents producing overlapping POIs, (2) timeline dedup using type+name key that missed cross-category duplicates. The fix adds a proper cross-category dedup in _merge_day_data (Python, line 1072) that runs before any rendering. The JS timeline dedup (line 2626) provides a second layer of defense. The rendered output shows zero duplicates across all 15 days.

code_quality_findings.issue: JS timeline dedup filter() cannot retroactively remove already-accepted items. If a lower-priority item (entertainment) passes filter before higher-priority item (attraction), both end up in output.
code_quality_findings.recommendation: Use reduce() or two-pass approach instead of filter(). Not currently triggered because Python dedup runs first, but would fail as standalone safety net.

code_quality_findings.issue: Original 9 cross-category duplicates still present in data files. Code-level dedup handles them, but data files are inconsistent with rendered output.
code_quality_findings.recommendation: Consider cleaning data files to match rendered output for consistency, though not strictly required since code dedup handles it.

all_findings.issue: JS timeline dedup uses filter() which cannot retroactively remove already-accepted lower-priority items. If entries arrive in non-priority order, both duplicates would pass. Currently mitigated by Python-level dedup running first.
all_findings.recommendation: Replace filter() with reduce() or two-pass approach for correctness as a standalone safety net.

all_findings.issue: Original 9 cross-category duplicates remain in data files. Code-level dedup resolves them in rendered output, but data files are inconsistent.
all_findings.recommendation: Clean data files to remove duplicates for consistency. Not blocking since code dedup handles them.
